name: TeamStarWolf - Impact: Destruction, Extortion & Disruption
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Scores are membership tiers (core=100, supporting=55), not severity, confidence, incident frequency, or a coverage guarantee. Technique IDs and tactic assignments are checked against official Enterprise ATT&CK 16.1 and the bundled 18.1 dataset; the layer retains v16-compatible tactic slugs. Core rows describe selected Enterprise impact behaviors; supporting rows describe access, preparation, collection and exfiltration that can precede destructive or extortion scenarios. Extortion is a scenario objective, not a standalone Enterprise ATT&CK technique or tactic. No actor attribution, mandatory attack sequence, or ICS coverage is implied. This is a planning view, not an instruction to execute destructive actions.

techniques.comment: Data Destruction. Core: Destroying business data can interrupt operations without involving encryption.
Data Encrypted for Impact. Core: Encrypting data can deny availability and create pressure in an extortion scenario.
Inhibit System Recovery. Core: Disabling or damaging recovery mechanisms can prolong an outage and complicate restoration.
Service Stop. Core: Stopping services can interrupt operations or remove obstacles to subsequent impact.
Account Access Removal. Core: Removing legitimate account access can prevent operators from administering affected systems.
Disk Content Wipe. Core: Wiping disk contents can irreversibly destroy data; use discussion or synthetic evidence in training.
Disk Structure Wipe. Core: Damaging disk structures can prevent boot or data access; use discussion or synthetic evidence in training.
Endpoint Denial of Service. Core: Exhausting or exploiting endpoint resources can deny service; inclusion does not imply every sub-technique is modeled.
Network Denial of Service. Core: Network denial of service can make a service unreachable; this is an outcome family, not a measured incident rate.
Internal Defacement. Core: Internal defacement can replace information visible to staff and interfere with trusted workflows.
External Defacement. Core: External defacement can alter public-facing content and damage trust.
System Shutdown/Reboot. Core: Unauthorized shutdown or reboot can interrupt service and impede recovery work.
Firmware Corruption. Core: Firmware corruption can render equipment unusable; retain as a discussion-only scenario in a home lab.
Stored Data Manipulation. Core: Stored-record manipulation can undermine integrity even when systems remain available.
Transmitted Data Manipulation. Core: Changing data in transit can corrupt decisions based on exchanged information.
Runtime Data Manipulation. Core: Runtime manipulation can alter results while an application is processing data.
Valid Accounts. Supporting: Abused accounts can provide access needed for later destructive actions; impact is not inevitable.

Unix Shell. Supporting: Unix-shell execution can orchestrate later actions on Linux or macOS; it is one possible execution path.
Disable or Modify Tools. Supporting: Impairing security tools can reduce detection before impact.
Group Policy Modification. Supporting: Abused Group Policy changes can distribute harmful configuration through a Windows domain.

Data from Local System. Supporting: Collecting local data can support theft-based extortion without requiring encryption.
Local Data Staging. Supporting: Staging data can prepare it for theft before an extortion demand.
Archive via Utility. Supporting: Packaging collected data can prepare it for transfer; archiving is not itself impact.
Exfiltration to Cloud Storage. Supporting: Unapproved cloud-storage uploads can export data later used as extortion leverage.
Exfiltration Over C2 Channel. Supporting: Data can leave over an existing command-and-control channel before impact occurs.

metadata.name: selection_rule
metadata.value: Core: selected Enterprise availability and integrity impacts, including encryption, wiping, recovery inhibition, disruption and defacement. Supporting: access and preparation plus collection/exfiltration that can support extortion. Tier is relevance to this lens, not severity.

metadata.name: score_meaning
metadata.value: 100=core; 55=supporting. Membership only, not severity, prevalence, confidence, or measured defensive coverage.

metadata.name: tactic_policy
metadata.value: Display each selected technique under all of its official 16.1 tactics, verified to match the bundled snapshot. Display expansion does not assert a scenario uses every tactic or requires every step. The app may translate retired IDs for its newer live matrix.

metadata.name: validation_source
metadata.value: Official Enterprise ATT&CK 16.1 and src/assets/data/enterprise-attack.json (collection version 18.1). The bundled file is not v16; both snapshots retain defense-evasion.
